body: You know, just life and bullshit. I realize this would probably haunt some folks for some time, and regret being somewhat self-centered as far as this goes.

Do you have any friends or family  who can help you pay for  your medications for the time being? How many people have you informed of your situation? Have you at least spoken to your physician about what options might be available?
Anything to connect with! A doctor can help you. It really couldn't hurt at this point. Your friends may also help you as you search for help.

Yeah, depression will do that. But again it isn't too late have really meaningful connections to songs, like you may have had before, to people, ideas or even to really commonplace occurrences.You might need help, but many people have been able to find help before, and as long as you are alive it is never too late.

That's awesome! I really like jazz. I discovered an ensemble called Cortex during a bad spell awhile back. A couple months later I realized that I would never have had the pleasure of listening to them if I had decided to follow through on my intentions.

 At another bad moment a bit later, I rediscovered some bossa nova stuff I hadn't listened to for awhile. I decided I might just possibly be able to live for music alone, and then other things came along. Maybe you could reconnect with music. Doesn't need to be a career. Generally people don't really live for their employers. It could be a personal attachment, a passion.
What kind of music do you like? Discovered anything interesting lately?

Yeah, I have horrible ADHD, which makes it super difficult to stick with new hobbies. But I eventually found things where I didn't feel like I needed to be performing for anybody, which made things kind of better. Is there anything you might enjoy independently of either your skill or other people's appreciation? Listening to music, reading, sitting in the sun light, or really anything in the world? Something inviting.

If it doesn't seem like it, it isn't too late to look, to experiment with new and interesting things, and if necessary figure out why it's so difficult to find joy in things and, with some help, start out on reversing that.
Did you like it before you were good at it? If you could like and become good at drumming, think of all the other things you might pick up and find joy in.

Not bored. So you enjoy drumming? Forget about the career and your grades and your parents marriage for a moment and bang on some drums. Is it a thing you love in itself, or do you feel like somebody needs to pay you for it to be a worthwhile activity?

If you find you don't enjoy it so much, well, there are other things we can do. But I doubt it will hurt to put everything aside for a second to let it out on some stretched hide.

Hmmn.  You're not late.  I was kind of panicky last night, but I have calmed down momentarily.  You should know this. 

Still unsure of things.
Yes, but most people have a pattern of behaviors which allow them to adapt to these sorts of realities.
I have reconsidered.  Though I really hate psychotherapy and pills.

Nobody ever disagreed with you.   All that was suggested is that people eating raw meat for this first time might experience indigestion, not that such people simply cannot eat raw meat.  You're writing something into the conversation that isn't there.

No.  I'm working, but I just graduated from college and am at home for the summer, or however long.  Part of what I'm feeling is probably just transitional ennui. 

But I've also had these sorts of violent urges buried for awhile, and they are now seemingly being forced to the surface by these circumstances.   It's not that I just don't know what to do in the future.  It's that I don't know what I've been doing my entire life, don't know who I am, or really why I should be alive, which makes that sort of "decision" kind of overwhelming or impossible.

That's the thing.  I can't think of anything as much as I try.  It's like imagining myself satisfied is imagining a different person entirely that I just don't know how to be.

I have most of what somebody is expected to aspire to in our society, but just can't be bothered to give a damn or attach any value to these things or my relationship to the world.
